title: deployment-surface-mapping-and-data-flow-notes
summary: Working notes from feasibility workshop: map customer environment surfaces, data flows, and block-level requirements for an air-gapped / isolated on‑prem Redwood Inference deployment. Focus on network topology, image distribution, secrets/KMS, telemetry constraints, and test surface for POC.
body:
Purpose:
- Capture the minimal viable surface and non‑functional requirements to run a small customer POC in an air‑gapped datacenter (3-node inference cluster + control plane + aux services).
- Provide a concrete checklist for Solutions Eng and Site Ops to validate before workshop signoff.

Assumptions (stated explicitly):
1) Customer wants NO outbound internet from the inference cluster.
2) Customer can provide a jump/offline bastion host that has scheduled controlled egress windows for bundle pulls (optional).
3) POC target hardware: 3 inference nodes with GPUs (customer will confirm model/VRAM), 1 control plane VM, 1 storage/registry node.
4) Customer accepts a signed offline bundle for images and packages; no live cloud calls for model downloads.

High-level topology (textual map):
- Management VLAN (control plane): control-plane VM (Redwood control services, web UI), RBAC + LDAP sync agent, local PostgreSQL for control metadata (single node for POC).
- Inference VLAN (compute): 3 x GPU worker nodes (container runtime + nvcr/registry mirror), NFS or local NVMe for model cache, metrics exporter.
- Registry/Artifact VLAN: internal OCI registry + package repo (APT/YUM) mirror, S3-compatible object store (minio) for model artifacts and quantized weights.
- Bastion / Sync Host (optional): controlled egress host used to pull update bundles from Redwood once per maintenance window.
- SIEM/Logging: filebeat/forwarder to customer SIEM over allowed network channel or local log aggregation only.

Data flows (who talks to whom):
- Control plane -> Worker nodes: gRPC/control messages (TLS mutual auth). Port list: control-plane 7443 (control), 9090 (metrics ingest optional).
- Worker -> Registry: OCI pulls for startup and model updates.
- Worker -> Object store: model weight fetch (signed objects).
- Metrics exporter -> (optional) Prometheus remote write endpoint or local prometheus scrape. If remote write is disallowed, store metrics locally and export via offline bundle.
- Admin workstation -> Bastion -> Control plane (SSH + port-forwarding for UI).

Network & Firewall requirements (POC minimal):
- Internal DNS for all nodes.
- NTP from customer time source (or no external NTP allowed; use hardware RTC sync).
- Allow inbound from control-plane IPs to worker node management ports only.
- Allow worker->registry (443/5000 depending on registry) within VLAN.
- Block all outbound 0.0.0.0/0 by default. Explicit egress for sync host if agreed.

Artifact distribution (airgap bundle model):
- Bundle components: OCI image tarballs (gzip tar), deb/rpm package archives, model artifact tarballs (sharded), install scripts, signed manifest.json (SHA256 + Redwood signing key).
- Recommended approach: deliver bundle on customer-approved medium (SCP over bastion, HTTP pull from internal staging, or physical USB on highly restricted sites).
- Bundle verification: control plane validates manifest signature before applying; worker nodes verify image digests on load.
- Typical bundle size considerations: base images ~6–12GB, base model weights variable (8–80GB depending on quantization). For POC pick small quantized model to keep bundle < 40GB.

Storage & model cache sizing notes:
- NVMe local cache (recommended): 1–2x model working set. If using 40GB weights, reserve 120–200GB per node for concurrent model shards and temp files.
- NFS/SMB for shared artifacts: OK for POC but not recommended for production model cache due to I/O variability.

Secrets, KMS, and HSM integration:
- Options: customer-managed HSM (PKCS#11), Vault (transit), or local sealed key store.
- For true airgap, prefer HSM or customer KMS. Redwood supports wrapping service keys for offline activation.
- Offline activation flow: Redwood issues a time-limited activation blob signed by customer key; control plane unseals with cluster-local HSM.
- Open item: confirm whether customer requires FIPS 140-2 validation and which HSM vendor (YubiHSM, Thales).

Telemetry & privacy constraints:
- Default: telemetry disabled unless explicit opt-in.
- Minimal telemetry for POC: health pings and anonymized usage counters stored locally.
- If export required, ship telemetry bundle via secure transfer to Redwood during maintenance window.

Upgrade and patch process (POC):
- Offline upgrades via new signed bundles.
- Pre-deploy canary: install on 1 worker; run smoke tests; if pass, rollout rest of nodes.
- Rollback: keep previous image tarballs on registry node for immediate revert.

Authentication and LDAP/AD integration:
- LDAP sync agent runs on control-plane VM and can write local service accounts.
- mTLS for service-to-service auth; client certs issued by customer PKI or cluster CA.

Test plan for POC (minimal):
1) Install verification: bundle integrity checks pass, control-plane starts, and worker nodes register.
2) Functional smoke: run 10 short text-generation requests, validate expected response structure.
3) Latency profile: 50 warm tokens at 16 concurrent sessions, measure p50/p95/p99.
4) Load sustain: 1 minute sustained QPS test at target throughput (customer to define).
5) Failover: simulate control-plane transient restart and verify worker reconnect and queued requests behavior.
6) Offline upgrade: apply new bundle on canary node and run regression evals comparing outputs to baseline (diff tolerance defined by product/POC).

Capacity planning quick reference (POC guidance):
- GPU: A100 80GB or 40GB recommended depending on model size; for small quantized models, 40GB may suffice.
- CPU: 16–32 cores per worker for pre/post-processing and batching overhead.
- RAM: 256GB recommended if using larger KV caches or multiple models.
- Disk: NVMe 1TB per node recommended for model cache + logs during POC.
- Network: 10Gb internal recommended between nodes for large shard transfers; 1Gb may be acceptable for small models.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Bundle corruptions during transfer -> Mitigation: use SHA256 manifest, retry with delta-sync tool.
- Risk: Customer policy forbids any signed remote manifest checks -> Mitigation: provide local manifest verification tools and reproducible build artifacts.
- Risk: HSM incompatibilities -> Mitigation: early HSM vendor validation and test harness prior to on-site POC.
- Risk: Insufficient NVMe leading to OOMs -> Mitigation: conservative capacity sizing and small-model quantized default for POC.

Open questions (requires customer answers before field visit):
- Which HSM/KMS vendor and model is available on-site? (YubiHSM/Thales/other)
- Do they allow a scheduled egress window for the bastion host? How often and how large can transfers be?
- Which GPU models (exact SKU) will be provided? Memory sizes? PCIe/NVLink topology?
- Is there an internal CA we must use for mTLS or can Redwood issue ephemeral cluster CA?
- SIEM/log retention: where do logs need to be retained and for how long?

Action items (owners + deadlines):
- [Marcus] Produce a 2–3 page POC runbook trimmed for customer site visit (due 2026-03-10).
- [Leah] Validate offline bundle builder size with a small quantized LLaMA-style model and report expected bundle sizes (due 2026-03-08).
- [Priya] Draft HSM compatibility checklist and required PKCS#11 ops (due 2026-03-12).
- [Tomás] Create a minimal prometheus/metrics retention design that works offline for POC and outline export tooling (due 2026-03-09).

Notes to field engineers (practical tips):
- Bring a pre-seeded USB with latest airgap bundle and verification keys; label devices and record checksums before shipment.
- Confirm power/cooling and GPU driver versions ahead of time; bring driver packages in the bundle.
- Prefer running disk and network benchmarks onsite before installing to set expectations.

Decision log / quick recommendations: (for workshop review)
- Default POC stance: do as much as possible locally and avoid any outbound traffic except via documented, auditable maintenance windows.
- Use signed offline bundles with manifest verification and keep telemetry off by default.

Appendix: quick checklist for customer pre-validation (one-pager style)
- Hardware inventory: hostnames, CPU, GPU SKU, RAM, NVMe size, network uplinks.
- Network: VLAN IP ranges, DNS, NTP source, firewall team contact.
- Security: HSM vendor, internal CA details, compliance requirements (FIPS/ITAR).
- Personnel: on-site admin contact, storage admin, network engineer, security owner.
- Logistics: preferred transfer method for offline bundle (SCP, physical media), available maintenance windows.

End of working notes. These are intentionally prescriptive but incomplete — aim is to use as a checklist in the pre-POC call with customer.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-18 created (initial capture from solutions-eng pre-call).
- 2026-02-27 updated with capacity guidance after infra team feedback.
- 2026-03-05 added action items and owner deadlines for field prep.
